scope_description.value: Energy benchmark (SEC) for three major paper product families (packaging, printing and writing, tissue) across three production scale groups, based on a national survey and energy audits of pulp and paper factories in Vietnam.
scope_description.evidence_quote:
I, therefore, focus on three major paper product families, including packaging paper, printing 
and writing paper, and tissue paper.

sector_registered.evidence_quote:
In this research, I established an energy benchmark for the pulp and paper industry of 
Vietnam.

mechanisms.evidence_quote:
Energy consumption of papermaking processes may vary by different pulps and different products 
and requires normalization.

As the product quality has not been compared, the lower SEC of group 1 is explained as the simpler process with fewer stages in the 
stock preparation section, which has been observed during the preliminary audits at the sample factories.

Therefore, the discrimination in energy 
consumption of DIP and non-DIP processes among the factories in Vietnam cannot be considered.

It has been noted that only group 2 of this subsector with 04 sets of data could be used for 
benchmarking exercise (Table 7).
mechanisms.mechanism_effect_on_model: insufficient data length for the model

adaptations.evidence_quote: The variation due to different pulp properties could be normalized by converting it into one main pulp.

it was finalized to carry out benchmarking per range of 
production scale for each sub-sector (i.e. packaging, tissue, writing and printing sub-sector).

study_limitations.evidence_quote:
In this research, I cannot get data 
from all factories in the industries and the number of audit factories can be increased to enhance the 
quality of results.

However, the 
consumption of different energy sources in different paper facilities has not been statistically 
reported.

It should be noted that only in Group 3 (small capacity category) under the packaging sub-sector, the total production capacity of the samples does 
not reach 35% of the total sub-sector capacity as required due to the low interest of the enterprises.

coefficients_given.evidence_quote:
The conversion factor 1.31 and 1.48 for different types of packaging products (testliner, standard 
medium, coasting testliner, chipboard, and coreboard) are obtained by audit results in RCEE_NIRAS 
and ENERTEAM [7].

reviewer_notes: This is a benchmarking study using specific energy consumption (SEC) as an intensity ratio, aggregated as mean SEC per scale group; no fitted regression, so estimation method, variable selection, in-sample fit and out-of-sample validation are treated as not applicable. Modelled as one multi-site application (Vietnam pulp & paper industry) with three sub-sector SEC models distinguished by their equivalent-production conversion formulas (Eqs 4-9). Note internal inconsistencies in reported saving potentials: section 3.4.1 gives 19.5% (packaging), 11.6% (tissue), 20% (printing/writing) for Scenario 1, while the Discussion (section 4.1) states 13.6%, 17.6% and 14.4% respectively; the section 3.4.1 figures were recorded. Table 8 gives Scenario 2 whole-subsector potentials of 19%, 9% and 29%. n_observations for tissue derived from Table 3 (10 surveyed); packaging from '20 factories' in preliminary audit text; printing/writing recorded as the 4 group-2 data points actually usable.
